title: == vs === and Truthy vs Falsy
intro: Two JavaScript quirks behind many beginner bugs. Here's how to stay out of trouble.

slides.heading: == (loose)
slides.subtitle: Converts types before comparing.
points: The conversion rules are easy to forget

slides.heading: === (strict)
slides.subtitle: No type conversion.
points: Type and value must both match
Predictable, so use it by default

slides.heading: Falsy values
slides.subtitle: The main values that count as false.

slides.heading: Watch out
slides.subtitle: Common surprises.
points: [] and {} are truthy, even when empty
Check array.length when testing for empty

scenario.situation: A form checks if (quantity == 0) to show an "out of stock" warning.
scenario.problem: An empty input gives "", and "" == 0 is true, so the warning appears before the user types anything.
scenario.fix: Check for an empty value first, then compare Number(quantity) === 0. Only a real 0 shows the warning.
scenario.takeaway: Use === and convert types on purpose.

cta: Which of these surprised you the first time?
